title: Lemon Chicken and Potatoes
seoTitle: Lemon Chicken and Potatoes | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Roast chicken thighs with oregano potatoes and pan jus
subtitle: Roast chicken thighs with oregano potatoes and pan jus
description: Bone-in chicken thighs roast over lemon-garlic potatoes until golden. Pan juices become the finishing sauce at the line.

steps.title: Heat oven and season potatoes
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss potato wedges with half the oil, oregano, salt, and pepper until evenly coated and lightly glossy on all sides.

steps.title: Arrange chicken over potatoes
steps.instruction: Nest seasoned chicken thighs skin-side up among potatoes on two half-sheets. Tuck lemon wedges and smashed garlic around the pan.

steps.title: Roast and baste
steps.instruction: Roast 35–40 minutes, basting once with pan juices, until chicken reads 165°F and potato edges turn golden and crisp.

steps.title: Deglaze pan juices
steps.instruction: Transfer chicken to a holding pan. Add broth to sheet pans, scrape browned bits, simmer on stovetop 2 minutes into a thin jus.

steps.title: Serve with parsley
steps.instruction: Portion chicken and potatoes, spoon jus over top. Potatoes should be tender inside with crisp exterior; chicken skin should crackle lightly.

proTips: Dry chicken skin thoroughly—moist skin never crisps in a hall oven.
Add halved cherry tomatoes last 15 minutes for color and acidity.
Feta crumble at the line adds salt without extra cooking.
tonightSpread: Horiatiki salad with cucumber and tomato.
leftovers: Shred chicken into a lemon-oregano wrap with potatoes.
Chop potatoes into a breakfast hash with eggs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sunday-roast energy on a weeknight. Potatoes soak up chicken fat and lemon for maximum flavor per bite.
mealPrepNotes: Par-boil potatoes 8 minutes for extra crisp edges if time allows. Station: Arrange potatoes in a single layer beneath chicken so they fry in rendered fat. Station: Rotate pans and baste chicken with pan juices halfway through roast. Station: Rest tray 5 minutes before portioning so juices redistribute into meat.
